question: Should OpenClaw add a canonical global `tools.exec.pty` default for exec calls, and what sandbox/approval constraints must it preserve?
rationale: The user problem is concrete, but the change adds a new shell-exec config default that affects operator expectations around PTY, sandbox suppression, and approval-backed gateway execution.

options.title: Approve Scoped Default
options.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an explicit opt-in default, keep per-call override precedence, keep sandbox PTY disabled, and require direct plus gateway approval coverage before merge.

options.title: Keep Per-Call Only
options.body: Do not add the config key; instead document that skills or callers must request `pty: true` per exec call when streaming output is needed.

options.title: Defer Into Exec UX Design
options.body: Hold this until maintainers decide the broader PTY, sandbox-warning, and shell-default config story across related exec issues.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Default
recommendation.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an explicit opt-in default, keep per-call override precedence, keep sandbox PTY disabled, and require direct plus gateway approval coverage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history signal for exec PTY behavior, fallback semantics, and the current config/runtime lines.
